nodes.label: Coverage gate --fail-under=78
nodes.rationale: CI fails the build if coverage drops below 78%, locking in the post-refactor 81% figure minus headroom; coverage is scoped to the eight local apps only.

nodes.label: Dummy Stripe/email env injection in CI
nodes.rationale: STRIPE_*, EMAIL_HOST_* and DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL have no defaults in settings/base.py, so a missing value raises at import time; CI must inject dummies for manage.py check and the test run to import at all.
nodes.norm_label: dummy stripe/email env injection in ci

nodes.label: WeasyPrint system dependency install step
nodes.rationale: PDF invoice generation via WeasyPrint needs pango/cairo/gdk-pixbuf native libs that are not in the uv-managed Python env, so the runner installs them with apt before uv sync.

nodes.label: djLint Django template hook
nodes.rationale: Templates are formatted with the django profile at indent 2; the hook is scoped with files: \.html$ so it only touches Django templates and not other markup.

nodes.label: Django static() returns [] when DEBUG=False
nodes.rationale: django.conf.urls.static.static() checks settings.DEBUG internally and silently returns an empty list in production, so media stops being served with no error; production must mount re_path + django.views.static.serve explicitly.

nodes.label: Coolify + Docker persistent volume MEDIA_ROOT
nodes.rationale: BASE_DIR resolves to /app/myshop inside the container (WORKDIR /app + repo root myshop/), so MEDIA_ROOT must be overridden to BASE_DIR.parent / 'media' to match the Coolify volume mounted at /app/media, otherwise uploads land outside the persistent volume and vanish on redeploy.

nodes.label: Two-layer i18n translation system
nodes.rationale: Static UI text and DB-authored content need different mechanisms: .po files can only cover strings known at makemessages time, so admin-entered products/posts are translated at render time instead.

nodes.label: |tr and |tr_safe template filters (i18n_extras)
nodes.rationale: Every template rendering product/category/post data must {% load i18n_extras %} and apply |tr, otherwise new admin-entered content silently stays Spanish in the English locale.

nodes.label: TranslationCache + DeepL cached translation
nodes.rationale: get_translation() returns text unchanged when the active language is Spanish (source language), hits the TranslationCache model first, and only calls the DeepL API on a cache miss — bounding API cost to one call per unique string.

nodes.label: AJAX favorites — live navbar badge (skUpdateFavBadge)
nodes.rationale: The badge is always set from the server-returned count, never DOM arithmetic, so three independent handlers (catalog, product detail, favorites page) cannot drift out of sync; both navbar badges render unconditionally and hide at 0 so they can update live.

nodes.label: Custom error handlers and the 502 limitation
nodes.rationale: Django has handler400/403/404/500 but no handler502, because a true 502 means the proxy cannot reach Django at all — no Django template can render. Workaround: Caddy rewrites a failed health check to /502/ while Django still runs, and serves a static body when it is truly down.
nodes.norm_label: custom error handlers and the 502 limitation

nodes.label: Working preferences (plan mode, TDD, task management, stack defaults)
nodes.rationale: Plan before tasks over 3 steps or architectural decisions, use subagents to save context, record every correction in tasks/lessons.md, never mark work complete without tests, and prefer the elegant fix over a patch.
nodes.norm_label: working preferences (plan mode, tdd, task management, stack defaults)

nodes.label: Pre-existing BlogPublicViewTests failures (4)
nodes.rationale: Tests assert "Public Post" appears in the response but the blog template no longer emits it — a template change that was never reflected in the test fixtures; classified as known-not-blocking rather than fixed inside the refactor.

nodes.label: CheckConstraint(check=) → condition= (Django 6)
nodes.rationale: Django 6 renamed the check= kwarg to condition=; legacy migrations (shop/migrations/0005_*, orders/migrations/0013_*) still pass the old kwarg. Valid under the pinned Django 5, deferred until the Django 6 upgrade because rewriting historical migrations is a larger change.

nodes.label: Per-phase baseline gate (no regressions allowed)
nodes.rationale: Each refactor phase must keep green tests >= 136, introduce no new failures/errors, and add no new manage.py check warnings — a numeric floor makes 'did we break anything' mechanically checkable.

nodes.label: Mono-repo shape (tooling at root, Django under myshop/)
nodes.rationale: Nearly every command needs cwd = myshop/ (Makefile targets cd for you); note the doubled name — myshop/ is the project dir and myshop/myshop/ is the settings/urls/celery package.
nodes.norm_label: mono-repo shape (tooling at root, django under myshop/)

nodes.label: Settings package (base + development/production/testing)
nodes.rationale: settings/__init__.py only branches production-vs-development, so pointing DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE at myshop.settings.testing bypasses the selector (Django imports the module directly) — that is why tests need the explicit env var or they hit the dev SQLite file.

nodes.label: Service layer (OrderService / AddressService / PaymentService)
nodes.rationale: Business logic lives in services, not views: create_order_from_cart() wraps order + OrderItem creation + cart.clear() in one transaction.atomic() so a partial order can never be committed, and cancel_order() also issues the Stripe refund.

nodes.label: Per-app managers.py query optimisation (with_full_details)
nodes.rationale: Prefer the queryset helpers over ad-hoc select_related in views — the N+1 audit was performed against the managers, so bypassing them re-introduces untested query patterns.

nodes.label: orders/views as a package with re-exporting __init__
nodes.rationale: __init__.py re-exports every view so `from orders import views; views.order_create` keeps working after the split; a new view must be added to its domain module AND to the re-export list.
nodes.norm_label: orders/views as a package with re-exporting __init__

nodes.label: Session-based cart (CART_SESSION_ID, coupon_id in session)
nodes.rationale: Cart.__iter__ prunes entries whose product was deleted from the DB, so no code may assume every session key still resolves to a Product; the applied coupon lives as coupon_id in the session rather than in the cart dict.

nodes.label: Celery for email and PDF side-effects
nodes.rationale: orders/tasks.py and payment/tasks.py run eagerly under the testing settings (CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER) so tests exercise the side-effects without a broker.
nodes.norm_label: celery for email and pdf side-effects

nodes.label: Redis sorted-set recommender with silent degradation
nodes.rationale: _get_redis() returns None when Redis is down so recommendations degrade silently instead of erroring the page — an optional feature must never take down the catalog.
nodes.norm_label: redis sorted-set recommender with silent degradation

nodes.label: accounts.CustomUser with regular/wholesaler user_type
nodes.rationale: is_wholesaler / is_regular drive wholesale pricing and the form-mayorista flow, so the user_type field is load-bearing beyond display.

nodes.label: i18n_patterns URL routing with deliberate exclusions
nodes.rationale: admin/, i18n/, ckeditor5/ and payment/webhook/ stay outside i18n_patterns because Stripe POSTs to a fixed unprefixed URL — moving the webhook inside would break payment confirmation; 502/ and maintenance/ are mounted both inside and out.
nodes.norm_label: i18n_patterns url routing with deliberate exclusions

nodes.label: Split media serving (static() under DEBUG, re_path otherwise)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate duplication: django.conf.urls.static.static() returns [] when DEBUG=False, so production needs an explicit re_path + django.views.static.serve.
nodes.norm_label: split media serving (static() under debug, re_path otherwise)

nodes.label: Translations — two layers (static .po + DB |tr)
nodes.rationale: Source language is Spanish (LANGUAGE_CODE=es); DeepL is bypassed when the active language is Spanish or DEEPL_API_KEY is unset, so the site stays functional without the API key.

nodes.label: myshop.utils.safe_next_url for ?next= redirects
nodes.rationale: A raw next parameter is an open redirect; three views were already fixed for this, so every new ?next= handling must route through the helper.

nodes.label: Resolver-Match Active Link Highlighting
nodes.rationale: The sidebar marks the current entry active by substring-matching request.resolver_match.view_name against namespaced URL names ('accounts:profile', 'orders:address', 'support:'). Prefix matching ('support:', 'orders:address', 'payment:payment_method') is deliberate so that all sub-views of a section keep the parent entry highlighted without listing every view name. Trade-off: substring matching can produce false positives if two namespaces share a prefix.

nodes.label: Flash Message Auto-Dismiss and bfcache Reload
nodes.rationale: Django messages are rendered into .sk-alerts and closed after 5s via bootstrap.Alert, with a plain element.remove() fallback in case the Bootstrap bundle failed to load. A separate pageshow listener force-reloads when event.persisted is true, so back/forward-cache restores do not show stale cart counts, favorite states or session-dependent badges.
nodes.norm_label: flash message auto-dismiss and bfcache reload

nodes.label: Multi-Brand Split: Synk Food vs Synk Beauty
nodes.rationale: One Synk is modelled as an umbrella brand with two storefronts. Synk Food is an internal Django route ({% url 'shop:synkfood' %}) while Synk Beauty is an external host (synkbeauty.dabg.dev) opened with target=_blank rel=noopener. Only the food catalogue lives in this codebase; the beauty brand is a separate deployment linked out, which keeps this project's models and checkout single-catalogue.
nodes.norm_label: multi-brand split: synk food vs synk beauty

nodes.label: Favorite Toggle AJAX Contract
nodes.rationale: Every favorite button POSTs to shop:toggle_favorite with X-CSRFToken plus X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest and expects a JSON body of {is_favorite, count}. A 401/403 response means anonymous, and the client redirects to accounts:login?next=<current path> instead of showing an error — this is why the view must answer with a status code rather than a redirect for AJAX callers. The returned count is fed to the global window.skUpdateFavBadge so the navbar badge stays in sync without a page reload.

nodes.label: user_favorites Context Variable
nodes.rationale: The grid pre-renders heart state with `{% if product.id in user_favorites %}`, so the view must supply user_favorites as a container of product IDs (not model instances) or every heart renders empty. This avoids one AJAX round-trip per card on first paint; the detail page uses a scalar `is_favorite` flag for the same purpose.

nodes.label: Category Image Slug Fallback Chain
nodes.rationale: When Category.image is empty the template falls back to hardcoded static art keyed on cat.slug ('dulces' -> sopa1, 'bebidas' -> sopa3, else sopa2). This hardcodes slug values into presentation: renaming a category slug silently changes its placeholder image. Same fallback chain is duplicated in synkfood.html with a different slug mapping ('bebidas'/'snacks').

nodes.label: Recetario Placeholder Cards
nodes.rationale: The {% empty %} branch renders six hardcoded demo cards pointing at a remote Unsplash photo and a dead href='#'. Marked in-source as 'tarjetas de prueba' — unshipped placeholder content that depends on an external CDN and should be removed once real Recipe rows exist.

nodes.label: Ticket Status Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Statuses are open / in_progress / waiting_customer / resolved / closed. 'closed' is terminal in the UI: the reply form and the Cerrar Ticket button are both hidden and the user is told to open a new ticket instead. Replying while in waiting_customer is expected to flip the ticket back to in_progress — the template announces that side effect, so the reply view owns the transition. Ticket.get_status_color supplies the Bootstrap colour, while priority colours are hardcoded in template if/elif chains in both detail and list.

nodes.label: Support Ticket List with Filters and Stats
nodes.norm_label: support ticket list with filters and stats

nodes.label: Ticket stats Context Dict
nodes.rationale: The stat cards read stats.open, stats.in_progress, stats.resolved and stats.total, so the list view must build a dict with exactly those keys. Filters are plain GET params (status, search, priority) re-echoed into the form via request.GET, meaning filter state survives without any session storage.

nodes.label: Error Pages Extend the Full Base Layout
nodes.rationale: All five error templates extend shop/base.html, which pulls in the navbar and footer includes and resolves {% url 'shop:product_list' %}. Django renders handler500 with an empty context and no context processors, so anything the base chrome needs from context (cart, favorites count, user) is absent — a template error inside the 500 page degrades to Django's bare fallback. Keeping the error pages branded costs that fragility.
nodes.norm_label: error pages extend the full base layout

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled Lead Form Without a Django Form
nodes.rationale: Fields (nombre, apellidos, email, telefono, estado, ciudad, comentarios) are raw HTML inputs posting to action='' rather than a bound Django Form, so validation is HTML5 `required` only and there is no server-side error rendering path — a rejected submission has nowhere to display messages. Copy also references a 'distribuidor Soho' brand that does not match the One Synk / Synk Food naming used everywhere else.
nodes.norm_label: hand-rolled lead form without a django form

nodes.label: Local Development Runbook
nodes.rationale: Scratch runbook: RabbitMQ 3.13.1-management as the Celery broker on 5672/15672, `celery -A myshop worker`, Flower with --basic-auth, Redis 7.2.4 on a non-default port 6378, and the Stripe CLI forwarding webhooks to 127.0.0.1:8000/payment/webhook/. The non-standard Redis port and the RabbitMQ-not-Redis broker choice are the details that break a fresh setup if assumed to be defaults.

nodes.label: Stripe Test Card Numbers
nodes.rationale: Success 4242…, decline 4000 0000 0000 0002, 3D Secure challenge 4000 0025 0000 3155 — the three checkout paths the payment flow is expected to handle.

nodes.label: Pinned Dependency Lock (uv pip compile)
nodes.rationale: Autogenerated from pyproject.toml by `uv pip compile`, so it is a lock artifact — edits belong in pyproject.toml, not here. Pins Django 5.0.14 (LTS-line) against a much newer transitive set.

nodes.label: WeasyPrint PDF Generation
nodes.rationale: WeasyPrint 68.1 plus its native chain (cffi, pydyf, pyphen, fonttools, tinyhtml5) — invoice/PDF rendering that needs system libraries present in the deploy image, the heaviest non-Python dependency in the lock.

nodes.label: Production Serving Stack (gunicorn, whitenoise, dj-database-url, psycopg2, sentry-sdk)
nodes.rationale: Gunicorn + WhiteNoise (static files served from the app process, no separate CDN/nginx static tier), Postgres via dj-database-url URL config, python-decouple for env vars, Sentry for error reporting — a single-container PaaS-shaped deployment.
